payload.question:
## Context

Research (docs/history/dispatch-config-cache/RESEARCH.md) confirms the item's config-re-read claim is real (`ensureRunnerConfigForDir` at src/runner/dispatch/config.mjs:245-274 does an unconditional `fs.readFileSync` with zero caching), but two parts of the proposal do not hold up:

1. The redundant `resolveExecutorAndOverrides()` call is real ONLY in `decideExecutorCli`'s `--work` door (src/runner/dispatch/cli.mjs:668 then :695, same cfg/executorId). The `executeExecutorCli` door's own version of this exact bug was already fixed -- its own code comment at cli.mjs:392-404 documents a prior fix removing a second call there. "2-3 times" overstates the general case.

2. The proposal's headline motivation -- "10 agent ~70-150ms cumulative" saved under fan-out via a per-process cache -- cannot work as designed. `.claude/settings.json:24` registers `scripts/dispatch-decide-hook.mjs` as `node ".../dispatch-decide-hook.mjs"`, meaning Claude Code spawns a FRESH node process per Agent/Task-tool call (confirmed: this is how every PreToolUse hook fires). Every CLI door (`decide`/`execute` via `bin/fgos.mjs`) is likewise a fresh process per invocation. A per-process, module-level cache resets to empty on every one of these -- it cannot deliver savings across N separate Task-tool calls in a fan-out, only within a single process handling multiple calls internally (which, checked, mostly already happens correctly: `fanoutBatchExecutorCli` already reads config once at cli.mjs:741, before its per-candidate loop).

3. The item cites "D3 no-trust guarantee" as the safety justification for adding this cache. `grep -rn "no-trust" docs/ src/` returns zero hits anywhere in the repo -- this decision cannot be located. Separately, per `.agents/skills/_shared/citation-format.md`'s own locked rule (decision 0017), a `D<n>` id may NEVER be cited outside its own feature's `docs/history/<feature>/CONTEXT.md` -- and tsk-4sr has no CONTEXT.md of its own (docsRef is unset). So the citation is out-of-scope by convention even setting aside whether "D3" exists.

## Why this matters

If the fix is scoped as originally proposed (a per-process cache to cut fan-out overhead), it will ship with zero measurable effect on its own stated motivating scenario, because the architecture it targets (fresh process per Task-tool call) makes cross-call caching structurally impossible without a persistent daemon or an on-disk/shared cache -- a materially bigger, riskier change than the "safe, read-only, no semantics change" framing in the item description. A person needs to decide: (a) narrow scope to the one real, small, safe win -- memoize the two redundant resolveExecutorAndOverrides calls inside decideExecutorCli's --work door -- and drop the cross-process caching claim entirely, or (b) accept the larger scope of a real cross-process cache (daemon or on-disk, with real invalidation/staleness tradeoffs) to actually chase the fan-out savings. Also needs someone who knows what "D3 no-trust guarantee" was meant to reference (or confirmation it should just be dropped from the item's safety framing since it can't be verified or cited under the repo's own D-local citation rule).
